test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Sept 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the amount (in Rs.) due on a sum of money Rs. 12,500 after one year if the compound interest is payable half-yearly at 12% per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate per half-year = 12% ÷ 2 = 6%, Time = 2 cycles.

Effective CI rate for 2 cycles = 6% + 6% + (6 × 6)/100 = 12.36%

Amount = Principal + Interest = 112.36% of 12,500

⇒ Amount = 1.1236 × 12500 = 14045

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14,045.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53be02f06619df2722cab1acf08d715c68e90b73611ef4d6ae1bc7a66d2c9e69.png] 

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹12,500

Rate (R) = 12% per annum ⇒ 6% per half-year

Time (T) = 1 year ⇒ 2 half-years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount = 12500 × (1 + 6/100)²

⇒ Amount = 12500 × (106/100)²

⇒ Amount = 12500 × (53/50) × (53/50)

⇒ Amount = 12500 × (2809/2500)

⇒ Amount = 5 × 2809

⇒ Amount = 14045

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14,045.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 (R/2) and the given time period in years is multiplied by 2 (2T) to get the number of cycles.

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 successive periods at rate r%, the combined effective compound interest rate is directly calculated as: r + r + (r × r)/100.

Difference Between CI and SI

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly 2 cycles is calculated by the direct formula: D = P × (R/100)².
